results.title: DAGs in econometrics: a personal journey
results.content: 🔍 Key highlights from Microeconometrics with R: ⚙️ Unified frameworks for linear, nonlinear, and limited dependent variable models using R packages (lm, glm, plm, lme4, etc.) 📊 Integration of panel-data econometrics, fixed and random effects, and clustered inference 🧠 Causal inference approaches — DiD, matching, instrumental variables, and treatment-effect models 🌍 Application of semiparametric and nonparametric techniques for flexible modeling 📈 Emphasis on visualization, diagnostics, and reproducibility within R Markdown and broom workflows 🤖 Practical use of simulation, bootstrap, and resampling for robust empirical inference What sets Microeconometrics with R apart is its open-science orientation — combining econometric rigor with computational reproducibility, ideal for researchers, educators, and policy analysts.
